fields.expected: A sixth example is Gloria, an AI memory companion I built around neurodegenerative disease and reminiscence therapy. I wrote the full stack myself, React and TypeScript on the front end and Python with Flask on the back end. The retrieval layer combined OpenAI embeddings, Pinecone vector search, and a Neo4j graph so that memories and the relationships between people, places, and events could both be searched semantically and traversed structurally. The part I would point to for this role is the structured conversation state machine I built, which moved each interaction through explicit stages: prompting, drafting, refinement, and finalization. I did that because free-form LLM conversation drifts, and users working through a memory need the system to know where it is in the process rather than improvising. The broader lesson carried into later work: automation should help someone interpret and keep control of their own information, not quietly replace their judgment.
